events.assessment: The alert flags transaction 3626720 for $409.30 due to a real-time risk score of 0.69. Historical precedents show that similar high-scoring alerts, such as CC-5203 and CC-2354, are frequently cleared as legitimate once cardholders confirm travel or billing region alignment.
key_points: Multiple historical cases, including CC-5203, CC-2354, and CC-4230, involved high risk scores (ranging from 0.82 to 0.92) that were cleared after cardholders confirmed travel to the billing region.
Prior investigations like CASE-2016-HHF-015 and CASE-2016-HHF-012 demonstrate a pattern of clearing transactions when they align with billing regions or typical cardholder behavior.

events.claim: The transaction model, trained on the bank's own closed cases from July to October (its July-September version scored AUC 0.972 on October), scores this transaction 0.002, against a 2.0% base rate. It reads the unnamed Vesta C/D/M/V columns, the identity record, running aggregates of the resolved account and the graph's memory of earlier closed cases, all as known at transaction time. January activity is newer than anything the model learned from and carries patterns it has never seen, so a low score counts at most as weak evidence of innocence: its weight is bounded to between 0.5 and 8

The alert's score (0.69, as in the case record) differs from the score stored on the transaction (0.11). Two bank sources disagree, and neither moves the decision: the bank warns its model is near useless for January, so its score is not used as evidence
$409.30 is a typical amount for this card (percentile 77%)
This card has 5 earlier purchases billed to region 203 (first on 2016-08-27)

Other charges on this card, not the flagged transaction, match the recipient surge pattern: This card's online purchase(s) ($181.16, $140.59) went to recipient e-mail domain sc.rr.com, which 17 different cards paid in the 30 days before this case, against a median of 2 card(s) a month in the earlier months it was paid at all: many cards paying one recipient. This signature never touched a cleared customer in July-December, so it conflicts with the clean flagged purchase: the case goes to an analyst under R8 instead of being closed
